name: Tunnel Records
note: Matched to the Tunnel Records shop inside the 4 Star Theater on Clement Street (about 150 m away).

facts.text: A sister shop of the Taraval Street store, set inside the renovated 4 Star Theater.
Opened in 2017 by founder Ben Wintroub.
The original store leans toward rare groove and obscure sounds.
A two-level bar with a balcony whose table-high windows look out onto the Stockton Tunnel.
Has customer-contributed artwork on display.
Opened in 2010 in a building that was a meat packing facility in 1917.
Occupies a historic brick warehouse across three levels.
First opened in 1935.
Designated a San Francisco Landmark on February 6, 2013.
Taken over in 1972 by Mary Ellen Cunha and Peggy Forster, who later removed the window coverings.
The building was constructed in 1883 and has a 1923 Mediterranean revival facade.

Run by the Seaglass restaurant team, with chef Loretta Keller as partner and culinary director.

name: Variety Club Preview Room
note: Yelp title: 'VARIETY CLUB PREVIEW ROOM - CLOSED - Updated January 2026 ... 582 Market St'.

facts.text: Founded in 1916 by Italian-American men led by George Gaggetti and named after composer Giuseppe Verdi.
Moved into its Mariposa Street building in 1935.
Began as a social club for people of Italian descent, with a soccer team and a baseball team in the late 1920s.

note: No address; matched to Victory Hall & Parlor at 360 Ritch St (Mission Bay/SoMa, same coordinates area).

facts.text: Housed in a building established in 1908 that once held the St. Francis Pie Company and the 330 Ritch nightclub.
Little Skillet opened a food counter inside the bar in January 2014.
